reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to confirm target engagement of either PD-1 or intratumoral IL-12. However, the combination therapy includes nivolumab (established PD-1 inhibitor) at standard dosing (480mg Q4W) and electroporation-mediated IL-12 delivery, suggesting likely target engagement. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to confirm downstream biology changes from checkpoint blockade or IL-12-mediated immune activation. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Strong clinical signal with 52.9% pathologic complete response rate (9/17 patients) in neoadjuvant melanoma, which is clinically meaningful. Additional supportive endpoints include 58.8% ORR, 93% 1-year RFS, and 94% 1-year OS. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported in this small single-arm study. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Single-arm design limits interpretation, but the pCR rate appears favorable compared to historical controls. High rate of serious adverse events (multiple SAEs across 56% of patients) but no dose modifications reported, suggesting tolerability was manageable.
